clue.text: Duplicate drain

definitions.meaning: to make copies of a document, as on a copier, is to run them off
a drain or overflow channel carrying surplus water away from land

explanation.definitionFit: Copying a document is running it off on a machine, and water draining off land is called its runoff.

clue.text: Steal stock out of bed to produce when needed

parts.note: to rustle is to steal cattle or other livestock
someone who is up has got out of bed

explanation.surface: A cattle thief rises from bed ready to raid a herd whenever it suits.
explanation.definitionFit: To rustle something up is an idiom for making or finding it quickly at short notice.

clue.text: Academic distinction gained by Pole to any extent

parts.note: the North Pole; Nth is a standard abbreviation of north
a degree is the qualification a university awards

explanation.surface: A Polish student earns a university qualification by sheer effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' suggests a person from Poland, but it is the North Pole, abbreviated Nth; 'gained by' just joins it to the degree.
explanation.definitionFit: To the utmost or any possible extent is an idiom: something taken to the highest degree imaginable.

clue.text: Fruity sweet made by kid

definitions.meaning: a cold dessert of puréed fruit folded into cream or custard, gooseberry being classic
to kid someone is to trick or tease them

explanation.definitionFit: The British pudding of crushed fruit and cream shares its name with the verb for deceiving a person.

clue.text: Get up to parade before a member

indicators.note: the display comes first, ahead of the article and the limb

parts.note: to parade something is to show it off
a limb such as a leg is a member of the body

explanation.surface: An instruction to rise and strut about in front of a limb.
explanation.walkthrough: SHOW A LEG is an old British call to get out of bed, originally a naval wake-up order.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is an idiom ordering sleepers to rise and get moving.

clue.text: Make a ton for part of county

definitions.meaning: a ton is slang for a century, a score of one ..., as in cricket
in old England a county was divided into administrative districts of this name

explanation.surface: A cricketer scores a century somewhere in the shires.
explanation.definitionFit: A ton is one hundred, and historic English shires were split into subdivisions called hundreds.

clue.text: Way off target feast looks common

parts.note: a shot that is wide misses its target
a spread is a lavish meal laid out on a table

explanation.surface: A banquet that has missed the mark looks thoroughly ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: Something prevalent and found everywhere is widespread, which is what common means here.

clue.text: Beast goes 50-50 with a parent

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so two fifties give two Ls
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: An animal splits everything evenly with its mother.
explanation.walkthrough: '50-50' reads as half shares, but it is two Roman fifties, L and L.
explanation.definitionFit: A South American camelid kept for wool and carrying loads is a beast.

clue.text: Get together in fold

definitions.meaning: to collect or assemble, as people do at a meeting
in sewing, to draw fabric into small pleats or puckers

explanation.definitionFit: Assembling people is gathering them, and pleating cloth by drawing a thread is also called gathering.

clue.text: Give concrete form to first person upset over mass

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so the pronoun is written bottom to top

parts.note: me is the first person pronoun
a body is a mass, as in a body of water

explanation.surface: Someone flips out above a great heap of material and tries to make it solid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ME into EM, which sits 'over' BODY in the down grid.
explanation.definitionFit: To give an idea a tangible shape is to embody it, making abstract things real.

clue.text: Train chap to be a theologian '

parts.note: to school someone is to train or teach them
a man is a chap

explanation.surface: Coaching a fellow so he becomes a divinity scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: A medieval university scholar teaching scholastic philosophy and divinity was called a schoolman.

clue.text: Doctor receives a paper money order

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times newspaper, the paper printing this puzzle

explanation.surface: A physician is handed a newspaper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'receives' only links: DR, A and FT simply follow one another.
explanation.definitionFit: A banker's written order to pay a sum is a draft, a kind of cheque.

clue.text: Willingly tell story to small female

parts.note: to tell a story can mean to lie
F is the abbreviation for female

explanation.surface: Gladly spinning a yarn to a little girl.
explanation.walkthrough: LIEF is an old word meaning gladly, as in 'I would as lief stay'.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic adverb meaning gladly or readily, surviving in 'would as lief'.

clue.text: Regret country is in poor shape

parts.note: to be sorry is to feel regret
a state is a country or nation

explanation.surface: A nation that apologises finds itself in a bad way.
explanation.definitionFit: A deplorable condition is idiomatically called a sorry state.

clue.text: Shrewd firm led

parts.note: hard means firm or solid
to head a group is to lead it, so headed means led

explanation.surface: A tough company was run by a sharp operator.
explanation.definitionFit: A practical, unsentimental person who is not easily fooled is hard-headed, that is astute.

clue.text: Reluctant to be rude — nay perverse

indicators.note: perverse means contrary or twisted, so the letters are turned into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone unwilling to be impolite simply refuses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perverse' shuffles RUDE and NAY into UNREADY; UNREADY in old use means slow or hesitant, as in the English king Ethelred the Unready.
explanation.definitionFit: Being unprepared or hesitant to act matches reluctant in older usage.

clue.text: Manage to go straight

definitions.meaning: to manage people or a project is to be in charge of them
going by the shortest route, without detours

explanation.definitionFit: To manage is to direct, and a route without deviations is direct, the same as straight.

clue.text: Stop breathing on feathers of swallow with difficulty

parts.note: to choke is to be unable to breathe
down is the soft fine feathering of birds

explanation.surface: A swallow struggles for air with its plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: Forcing food down unwillingly is the idiom choke down, eating something with effort.

clue.text: Chief point of first night

parts.note: premier means chief or foremost
E for east, one of the compass points

explanation.surface: The headline moment of an opening performance.
explanation.walkthrough: A compass point is a crossword staple for N, S, E or W; here it is E.
explanation.definitionFit: The opening performance of a play or film is its premiere.

clue.text: Ridicule has cause to rise

definitions.meaning: to mock by parody or imitation
to make something go upwards, like a rocket

explanation.definitionFit: A parody that mocks someone sends them up, and launching something skyward also sends it up.

clue.text: After husband who takes a regular correspondence course

definitions.text: who takes a regular correspondence course

parts.note: post- is a prefix meaning after
man is used for husband, as in man and wife

explanation.surface: A married student following a postal study scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'correspondence course' is a mail carrier's daily round, not distance learning.
explanation.definitionFit: A letter carrier follows a fixed delivery route every day, taking the mail along it.

clue.text: Support outside left with relish

indicators.note: the backing word goes round the outside of the single letter

parts.note: to favour someone is to back or support them

explanation.surface: Backing the political left with gusto.
explanation.definitionFit: Relish can mean a tang or savour, which is taste or flavour.

clue.text: Fly one stumbling into crime

indicators.note: stumbling suggests something tripping and falling into disorder, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An insect blunders into wrongdoing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stumbling' rearranges FLY and ONE; 'into' links them to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious offence in law, graver than a misdemeanour, is a felony.

clue.text: Lancashire town loses northern end very quick

indicators.note: the town drops a letter from its spelling

parts.note: Preston is a town in Lancashire, in northwest England

indicators.note: the end of the word northern is its final letter

explanation.surface: A northern English town gives up its far end.
explanation.walkthrough: The end of 'northern' is N, which PRESTON 'loses' from its own end. PRESTO is the musical term for a fast tempo.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, presto marks a very fast tempo, and it also means suddenly or rapidly.

clue.text: Series of games only with footpad

parts.note: a rubber is a match of several games, as in bridge or tennis
sole means only, as in the sole survivor

explanation.surface: A run of matches against just a highwayman.
explanation.walkthrough: A footpad is an old word for a robber on foot; here it is read as a pad under the foot.
explanation.definitionFit: A bottom layer of rubber on a shoe cushions the foot like a pad.

clue.text: Dip into graduate article

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a graduate
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: A new graduate takes a plunge into an item.
explanation.definitionFit: To bathe is to take a swim, or a dip, in water.

clue.text: Breadth of support for building

definitions.meaning: a ship's width at its widest point
a long horizontal timber or steel member holding up a structure

explanation.definitionFit: A vessel's width is its beam, and a horizontal girder in a structure is also a beam.

clue.text: Hang on incase

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Hang on incase': the OCR runs 'in case' together, so the second definition 'case' (a grip, a travelling bag) is not a word of the clue as held

clue.text: Put in position to take chair before newsman

parts.note: to take a chair is to sit down
ed is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: Seating oneself ahead of the journalist.
explanation.definitionFit: Something placed in a location is sited, located there.

clue.text: Youth has to register sound of small part

parts.note: a minor is a young person under the age of majority

indicators.note: sound signals that the word for register is heard, not spelt, giving a word with the same pronunciation

parts.note: a roll is a register or list of names

explanation.surface: A young person signs up to hear a little acting.
explanation.definitionFit: A minor role is a small part in a play or film.

clue.text: Finished twice exhausted

indicators.note: twice signals that the word finished supplies two synonyms in turn

parts.note: over means finished, as in the game is over
over means finished, as in the game is over

explanation.surface: Something done with, twice over, and worn out.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone can mean overworked or worn out, like exhausted.

clue.text: Cadge cake

definitions.meaning: to scrounge or beg from others

explanation.definitionFit: A scrounger sponges off friends, and a light Victoria-style cake is a sponge.
